title: IN-RS-CODE-004's gate proxy reads a nested generic ending in String as Result<T, String>
body:
The Rust critic's rule IN-RS-CODE-004 (no `Result<T, String>`) is enforced at the pre-commit gate by a greppable proxy, and the proxy reads a nested generic whose inner type ends in `String` as a `Result` whose error is a `String`.

Seen 2026-09-17 at the landing of ST0076's level-3 core: the gate refused `Store::resolution_basis` in `native/rust/crates/intentsvcs/src/store.rs` for

```
.collect::<Result<std::collections::BTreeMap<String, String>, rusqlite::Error>>()?;
```

whose error type is `rusqlite::Error`. The `String>, ` that closes the map's type parameters is what the pattern matched. cc moved the collection's type onto the binding (`let indexed: BTreeMap<String, String> = ... .collect::<Result<_, rusqlite::Error>>()?`) to get past the gate, and says `guide.rs` and `export.rs` already carry the same workaround for the same proxy. So three call sites have bent their code to a pattern, and the third did it at commit time, which made the landed bytes differ from the bank vc had judged (the difference was two lines and was verified by a tree diff).

What is wanted: the proxy does not fire on a `Result` whose error parameter is not `String`. The error parameter is the text after the LAST top-level comma inside `Result<...>`, so a pattern that cannot count angle brackets should at least require `, String>` to close the `Result` itself rather than an inner generic; the rule's Detection section says which, and one arm in the critic's own tests holds a nested-generic `Result` with a typed error as clean. The existing workarounds may stay or go; they are harmless.

Low. It costs a recomposition at the gate each time it fires, never a wrong program.

**CLOSED 2026-09-17, by the landing at 1740ddfb6, on vc's word.** IN-RS-CODE-004's two proxy patterns take `Result<[^<>]*, ` in place of `Result<[^>]*, `: a `Result`'s first parameter may hold no angle bracket, so a matched `, String>` or `, Box<dyn Error>>` always closes the `Result` itself and never a generic inside it. The `Result<BTreeMap<String, String>, rusqlite::Error>` that the gate refused now reads clean.

**The narrower of two fixes, on vc's ruling.** `[^<>]` is a subset of `[^>]`, so the new patterns can never strike a line the old ones did not, in this estate or in any consumer. What they stop striking is exactly this issue's class: an unclosed inner `<` before `, String>` means that `String>` closes the inner generic. The rule's Detection section now states the cost: a `Result` whose first parameter carries a generic, such as `Result<Vec<u8>, String>`, is not matched, a false negative.

**The proxy has always been blind to that shape**, because the old `[^>]*` stopped at the inner `>` too. Measured over every tracked `.rs` under a `src/` directory, the old patterns strike 0 lines, and a bracket-balancing pattern would newly strike six, which neither pattern ever caught: `render.rs:891` (`status_filter`, `Result<Option<Vec<ThreadStatus>>, String>`), `render.rs:5270` (`registered_roots`, `Result<Vec<PathBuf>, String>`), `render.rs:5953` (`entity_json`, `Result<Option<serde_json::Value>, String>`), `daemon.rs:735` (`parse_lsof_pids`, `Result<Vec<u32>, String>`), `graphql.rs:233` (the field `boards: Result<Vec<crate::model::Board>, String>`) and `legacy.rs:2595` (`satisfied_verdict`, `Result<(bool, Option<String>), String>`). Five of the six are private or crate-private functions or a field, which the rule's own "from public functions" does not call violations. Widening the pattern is a separate decision and is not filed.

**Guarded by one arm**, `a_string_closing_a_generic_inside_a_result_is_not_its_error_type` in `intent-cli/tests/critic_surface.rs`. It drives the binary against the real rule library over a five-line `src/lib.rs` and asserts that the rule strikes exactly the `String`, `()`-with-`String` and `Box<dyn std::error::Error>` lines, with the store.rs line clean and `Result<Vec<u8>, String>` pinned as not firing. It was red with the old RULE.md (struck lines 1 to 4 against 2 to 4) and green with the fix.

**The fix is in force at its commit**: the headless runner reads the rule library live from this tree, where `~/.local/share/intent/home` points, and no installed copy of the rule exists to sync. The three call sites that bent their code to the old pattern (store.rs, guide.rs, export.rs) stay as they are.
